dedupe_keys.name: drought water management and social equity analysing cape town s water crisis and day zero frontiers in water 2022

description: This open-access article analyses the 2015 to 2018 drought in Cape Town, which culminated in the city's notice of Day Zero in 2018, when taps were to be turned off. It compares daily rainfall with the levels of the Big Six supply dams from 2010 to 2021 and finds only a slight relationship, r squared 0.3 with a 3-month lag, pointing to rising water use and management decisions as causes; it also tabulates the measures the city adopted in 2017 and 2018 and rates which worked best. It notes that the population grew from 2.4 million in 1996 to 4 million in 2017 while dam storage grew about 15 percent, and concludes the crisis raised the financial burden of low-income communities. Coverage: one city, with data links in an appendix. Access: free open access text; the licence is CC BY. Caveats: correlation analysis with public data, not a hydrological model. It supports drought demand management and equity analysis for supply systems, and relates to the Singapore four national taps and Orange County reuse case studies in the catalogue.
